post_adjudication_public_state.title: Decision-Driven Orthogonal Learning with Complementary Feature Mining for Robust Synthetic Image Detection
post_adjudication_public_state.abstract: The widespread and inconsistent compression applied by Online Social Networks severely degrades the performance of synthetic image detectors. We attribute this degradation to two main issues: 1) the model confuses forgery artifacts with compression artifacts, and 2) compression erodes crucial discriminative high-frequency details. Existing methods suppress compression features during training but overlook the overlap between compression features and forgery-related features, leading to the unintended removal of forgery traces. To address artifact confusion, we introduce a Decision-Driven Orthogonal Constraint, which defines a classification decision axis pointing from the real class centroid to the forged class centroid. This constraint enforces compression artifacts to be orthogonal to the decision axis, mitigating their interference with forgery detection without entirely removing them, thus preventing the suppression of forgery-related features. To mitigate the erosion of high-frequency details, we propose to mine complementary forgery cues from both low-frequency information and compressed high-frequency components. A bidirectional update strategy and an adaptive global-local modulator are proposed to facilitate the utilization of forgery cues. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art generalization performance in challenging open-world detection scenarios.

labels_objectives_and_outputs.finding: An image encoder and shared text encoder form main-label and secondary-label image–text similarity matrices. Image-axis and text-axis contrastive terms align matched image/text pairs and suppress unmatched pairs. Overall loss adds both main terms and lambda times both secondary terms; lambda is 0.1. C is the number of distinct textual labels in the batch, not a stated generator-class count. ResNet50x64 plus Text Transformer is selected.

The linear probe trains a small added linear layer over the frozen image encoder with binary cross-entropy for real and synthetic subsets. Figure5(b) visibly labels the outputs Real and Synthetic. The text encoder is training supervision; it does not introduce a generator-ID inference head.

The alternative nearest-neighbor-style text matching uses the two text embeddings for Real and Synthetic. Its softmax produces the probability that a query image is synthetic from those two similarities. The defined matching is not nearest-generator retrieval.

The additional zero-shot feature test expects higher similarity within synthetic images or within real images than across authenticity categories. It remains authenticity representation/detection evidence; it does not test shared-generator identity among already-synthetic images.

post_adjudication_public_state.title: Generalizable Synthetic Image Detection via Language-Guided Contrastive Learning
post_adjudication_public_state.abstract: The heightened realism of AI-generated images can be attributed to the rapid development of synthetic models, including generative adversarial networks (GANs) and diffusion models (DMs). The malevolent use of synthetic images, such as the dissemination of fake news or the creation of fake profiles, however, raises significant concerns regarding the authenticity of images. Though many forensic algorithms have been developed for detecting synthetic images, their performance, especially the generalization capability, is still far from being adequate to cope with the increasing number of synthetic models. In this work, we propose a simple yet very effective synthetic image detection method via a language-guided contrastive learning. Specifically, we augment the training images with carefully-designed textual labels, enabling us to use a joint visual-language contrastive supervision for learning a forensic feature space with better generalization. It is shown that our proposed LanguAge-guided SynThEsis Detection (LASTED) model achieves much improved generalizability to unseen image generation models and delivers promising performance that far exceeds state-of-the-art competitors over four datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/HighwayWu/LASTED.

before.title: Decision-Driven Orthogonal Learning with Complementary Feature Mining for Robust Synthetic Image Detection
before.authors: Kai Li; Wei Wang; Linchao Zhang; Siying Zhu; Wenqi Ren
before.raw_venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
before.abstract: The widespread and inconsistent compression applied by Online Social Networks severely degrades the performance of synthetic image detectors. We attribute this degradation to two main issues: 1) the model confuses forgery artifacts with compression artifacts, and 2) compression erodes crucial discriminative high-frequency details. Existing methods suppress compression features during training but overlook the overlap between compression features and forgery-related features, leading to the unintended removal of forgery traces. To address artifact confusion, we introduce a Decision-Driven Orthogonal Constraint, which defines a classification decision axis pointing from the real class centroid to the forged class centroid. This constraint enforces compression artifacts to be orthogonal to the decision axis, mitigating their interference with forgery detection without entirely removing them, thus preventing the suppression of forgery-related features. To mitigate the erosion of high-frequency details, we propose to mine complementary forgery cues from both low-frequency information and compressed high-frequency components. A bidirectional update strategy and an adaptive global-local modulator are proposed to facilitate the utilization of forgery cues. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art generalization performance in challenging open-world detection scenarios.
